name: Ziphion
overview: Ziphion was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known specifically as a son of Gad. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational family groups in Israel's early history. The biblical record also associates him with the Zephonites, indicating his descendants or clan within the tribe of Gad.
namesAndTitles: The name Ziphion likely means 'gaze' or 'look out [tower], watch,' reflecting a possible characteristic or role. He is also called Zephon, a name meaning 'north' or 'northern,' which may relate to geographical or tribal distinctions. Both names are proper names found in Scripture but were not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ziphion as a son of Gad, affirming his place in the genealogical line of Israel. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ziphion's significance lies in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. His inclusion among those who went to Egypt connects him to the broader narrative of Israel's sojourn and eventual deliverance. The mention of the Zephonites in the census underscores the lasting identity of his lineage within the nation of Israel.
